title: IET equal-bin occupancy stays within 1 of L/m
statement: For the rotation {k θ} with θ = log2(3/2)/log2(3), every equal-width bin I of the circle, and every leftover length L, the occupancy satisfies |#I - L μ(I)| ≤ 1.
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / exponent-walk optimal control
tested_range: equal bins m=250 on leftover L at floor 26254995; high-precision confirmation at L=180467; extra L=19,84,1054,50508,60000,100000
counterexamples: L=180467, first bin [0, 1/250): 725 points against L/m = 721.868 (error 3.13); high-precision Decimal agrees
notes: The overshoot is concentrated in the first bin (u=0), the peak of the charge density. Other sampled bins at L=180467 sit at 721 (error 0.87). This is why Denjoy-Koksma at constant 1 failed on offsets and why a Riemann argument needs an occupancy cap h=4, not h=1. Published Ostrowski/Schoissengeier bounds on N D_N^* are too loose for the J-slack (partial quotients 23 and 55). Not a halt theorem.
